## CEO BRIEFING

**INC-2026-1109-01 — Batch API errors. State at 14:20 UTC: open, mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.**

**What happened**
From 11:42 to 12:58 UTC, some Batch API submissions returned 502 errors on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`. Errors were confined to one of the two Batch worker fleets; the other was clean throughout. Upstream storage was checked and ruled out at 11:47. At 12:58 we mitigated by cutting all Batch API traffic over to the healthy fleet. Error rate on the affected endpoint fell to 0.3–0.4% (baseline 0.2%) within two minutes and has held there.

**Where it stands**
- Incident policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before resolution. That verification window closes at **14:30**, so nothing is resolved, and cannot be called resolved, before then.
- Root cause is **not** established. Two candidate explanations are live (a connection-pool configuration change that shipped at 11:31, and concentrated load on the affected fleet from 11:38); neither has been tested. Engineering has deliberately not rolled the change back yet in order to preserve the evidence.
- The mitigation moved traffic; it did not fix the underlying fault. The affected fleet is still out of rotation.
- Engineering has not given a communicable completion time, and I would not offer one.

**Impact**
- Headline: **17,602 failed Batch API requests out of 58,900 Batch API requests** in the incident window — **29.9%**.
- Seven customer accounts affected: stark-industries, contoso, wayne-enterprises, globex, wonka-industries, umbrella-health, initech. (All seven sit on the affected fleet; that is an internal detail and not a reporting basis.)
- **Contoso** is the only affected account whose contract carries service credits. They have asked directly about Schedule B. Monthly Availability under their contract is calculated per calendar month across their Covered Services, determined from our own service records **after month end**, and published within 10 business days; claims run 30 days from that publication. We cannot confirm a breach today, and I would not speculate on a credit figure. Note their contract excludes requests failing through their own retry behaviour exceeding rate limits — their retry fix is written but still undeployed (their ticket TKT-8841), so some of their failures may fall under that exclusion. Any exclusion has to be published with its volume and basis, and is disputable by them.

**If it comes up on the board call**
Say: there was a Batch API incident starting 11:42 today; a mitigation was applied and the service is recovering; we are monitoring before confirming recovery; root cause is not yet confirmed and we will not claim one until it is; the one customer with a credit entitlement is being handled in line with their contract. Do **not** attribute a cause, describe a fix to the cause, give a resolution time, or describe the incident as resolved.

**Also**
Our 12:05 status-page update said the cause had been identified and a fix was rolling out. That was premature and wrong; a corrective public update goes out now. I am not putting anything on the status page about cause until engineering confirms one.

*Separate from this incident (internal only, not for the board discussion): SEC-411, a standing over-permission found in worker configuration during triage — no customer impact, no relation to this incident, ticket raised, Marcus owns, targeted this week.*

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**Handoff — INC-2026-1109-01. Current as of 14:20 UTC. Incident OPEN: mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.**

**Current state**
- All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b at 12:58. fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
- Error rate on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`: 0.3–0.4% at 14:12, against a 0.2% baseline. Queue depth on fleet-b normal.
- Verification window opened 13:00, closes **14:30**. Under incident policy, nothing is called resolved before it closes clean.
- No new customer failure reports since the cutover.

**Key timeline**
- 11:31 — `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` completed rollout to **both** fleets (three dependency bumps; max DB pool size per worker lowered 80 → 24).
- 11:38 — Batch submission volume on fleet-a climbs; ~3x morning average by 11:50, driven mainly by a large scheduled job from wonka-industries.
- 11:42 — First page, fleet-a 5xx rate. Incident start.
- 11:47 — Upstream storage provider ruled out (provider status green; Files API on same provider healthy).
- 12:31 — Decision: do not roll back `r3`; keep fleet-a state intact so the pool hypothesis can be tested. Mitigate by moving traffic. **Still the standing decision — rollback test has not been run.**
- 12:58 — Mitigation applied. 12:58–13:52 — re-drive of failed jobs in progress, ~60% through the affected accounts, no failures on re-drive.

**Live hypotheses (none tested)**
- **H1 — pool change in `r3` (leading).** For: pool 80→24 at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page; fleet-a workers observed queueing on database connections. Against: `r3` shipped to fleet-b as well and fleet-b never degraded.
- **H2 — concentrated load on fleet-a.** For: ~3x morning average from 11:38, single large scheduled job. Against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.
- Possible interaction between H1 and H2 — a third proposition, equally untested.
- **H3 — upstream provider. Rejected** at 11:47.

**Open items**
1. Root cause not established.
2. `r3` rollback test not run.
3. fleet-a still out of rotation, not returned to service.
4. Re-drive not finished (~60% at 13:52).
5. Resolution cannot be stated before 14:30 at the earliest.

**Next actions**
- Hold and watch to 14:30. If the window closes clean, decide the sequence for the rollback/root-cause test and the return of fleet-a to rotation — fleet-a is mitigated around, not fixed, so do not return it to rotation without a deliberate decision.
- Finish the re-drive and report completion.
- Keep this channel as the single source of truth on cause. Ruth has confirmed she will take anything published from Tomas' approved list only.

**Reporting**
Headline impact figure, from `customer-impact.csv` only: 17,602 failed / 58,900 Batch API requests in the window = **29.9%**. Do not report on a per-fleet basis — fleet membership is an internal deployment detail and is not a reporting basis.

**Out of scope** — SEC-411 (database role over-permission found during triage, no relation to this incident, no customer impact) is tracked separately, Marcus owns it.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**Subject:** Re: Batch submits failing — your impact and next steps [TKT-8903 / TKT-8907]

Hello,

Thank you for both of your tickets today, and for offering Priya Raghunathan's time — we have her contact details noted and will come straight to her if we need someone technical on your side.

**What happened to your account.** From 11:42 UTC today, some Batch API submissions returned errors. Between 11:42 and 12:58 UTC, 3,410 of the 9,400 Batch API requests your account made in that window failed. Your first failed request was at 11:43 and the last at 12:56.

**Current status.** We applied a mitigation at 12:58 UTC. Batch API error rates have returned to near-normal levels since then and have held. We are still monitoring before we confirm recovery — this incident is not yet resolved, and we will not describe it as resolved until our verification is complete. Other Northstar APIs are unaffected. Root cause has not been confirmed, and we will not speculate about it.

**On Schedule B and service credits.** I understand why you are asking, but we cannot confirm today whether November will fall below the 99.9% Monthly Availability commitment, or what credit would apply. Under your Schedule B, Monthly Availability is calculated per calendar month across your Covered Services and is determined by Northstar from our own service records **after the end of the calendar month**, with the figure published within 10 business days of month end. Any credit claim is then submitted within 30 days of that publication. One point I would rather flag now than surprise you with later: where we exclude requests under B.2 — including requests that failed through retry behaviour exceeding your contracted rate limits — we must identify the excluded volume and the basis for the exclusion in the published figure, and you may dispute an exclusion within the claim window. Our earlier note about your integration's immediate retries without backoff (TKT-8841, still awaiting deployment behind your Q4 freeze) is relevant to that. We will be specific and transparent about any exclusion we apply.

**Next update.** We will write again by 14:45 UTC with the outcome of our verification and anything further we can tell you.

Regards,
Northstar Support

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

## 2026-11-09 14:20 — Update on elevated errors on the Batch API

Since 11:42 UTC today, some Batch API requests have been returning errors. We have applied a mitigation, and error rates on the Batch API have returned to near-normal levels. We are monitoring before we confirm recovery.

Our 12:05 update said that we had identified the cause and were rolling out a fix. That was premature. We have not confirmed a root cause, and we will not publish one until it is confirmed.

We will post another update by 14:45 UTC.

*Monitoring.*
